language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I am Ellen Jansens, welcome to the beautiful city of Cape Town. Today we are going to explore the peninsula of the Kaap de Goede Hoop, or in English: Cape of Good Hope.
We will be heading down to the Plateau Road, the Reserve, the Cape Point, and finally to Cape of Good Hope.

We have a nice sunny day today! Did you know that even though plants and animals get their energy differently, the ultimate source of energy is always the sun? We'll learn more about this on our way! Let's go!
Ah! The Plateau Road is so scenic. Let’s look around. All organisms on earth need energy to live.
Some organisms, like plants, create their own energy. They are called ‘Producers’.
Some organisms need to eat other organisms to get energy. This group is called ‘Consumers’.
Fungi and some animals break down dead matter to create energy. They are called ‘Decomposers’.
Let’s see if you can identify if the following are Producers, Consumers, or Decomposers.

exercises.title: Where do animals get their energy from?

dialog.text: Look at the view from the reserve. I can see penguins in the distance! How do they get their energy?

Did you know that animals can either get their energy by eating plants or eating other animals, or eating both. Animals that eat only plants are called ‘Primary Consumers’ and animals that eat other animals are called ‘Secondary Consumers.

Animals that eat only plants are called ‘Herbivores’, animals that eat other animals are called ‘Carnivores’, and animals that eat both plants and other animals are called ‘Omnivores’. That’s a lot of different names huh?
